introduction: The Báb’s first eighteen disciples, whom He called the Letters of the Living, each had to find and recognize Him “spontaneously and of their own accord”. These readings give that condition, their names, the numerical symbolism built on them (nineteen with the Báb, the nineteen-day Feast, the twenty-four elders of the Apocalypse), and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s sober remark that the greatness of most of them “resides solely in the fact that they professed their faith at the very beginning”. The twelve apostles are the obvious parallel: Andrew’s “We have found the Messias”, the nets left behind, the restoring of the number after Judas, and Peter as the rock. Jesus’s “ye have not chosen me” and “many that are first shall be last” speak to the readings’ two themes of choosing and of rank.
questions: Why did the Báb require that His first disciples find Him without being told? What does unprompted recognition prove?
Reading 17 says the Letters’ glory is mostly that they were first. Is being first a spiritual merit?
Both the twelve and the eighteen included some who later fell away. What does that say about the security of any spiritual station?

outside.why: Eighteen souls must find Him of their own accord. Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias.
Unwarned and uninvited. Flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.
The Báb required that His first disciples seek Him out unprompted. Jesus told his: ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you. Are these two accounts of how disciples are made, or two sides of one?
The reading names them. And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach.
Singled out among the Letters. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
Eighteen and the Báb make nineteen. The eleven thought the number mattered enough to restore it: the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

The twenty-four chosen ones of the Apocalypse are explained as the Letters and others. Round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment.
The nineteen-day Feast named for the nineteen. Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel; and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them.
The first to believe was Mullá Ḥusayn. Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.
All the messengers and martyrs together. Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
The glory of most of the Letters lies solely in having believed first. But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.

Some of the first later fell. One of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests. What does it mean that both communities record the failure of some of their founders’ first companions?
Paul’s warning to the confident fits those who were first: let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
A petition for steadfastness accepted. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
